d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 4. The Temperate Region
d.notions: Frost, snow, short growing season, drought, forest fire, shelterbelt, greenhouse.
d.focus: Problems faced in the temperate region and the adaptations of people.
d.competence: Learners are able to explain how people adapt their houses, clothes and farming to a difficult climate, and apply this idea to their own environment.
objectives: Identify the problems faced by people in the temperate region.
Describe how people adapt their houses, clothes and transport.
Describe how farmers adapt to the problems of the temperate climate.
recall: Temperate farming includes mixed, dairy, grain, ranching and Mediterranean farming.
It is very productive thanks to machines, science and cooperatives.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: difficulties of winter in Europe.
situation: In January, heavy snow falls in a village in Canada. Roads are blocked, the water pipes freeze, and the farmer cannot take his animals out to graze.
The farmer's cousin, visiting from Garoua, wonders how people can live and farm in such a cold place.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that heavy snow and cold make life and farming very difficult in the Canadian village.
What happened because of the snow?
Roads were blocked, water pipes froze, and the animals could not go out to graze.
How can the farmer prepare for the next winter?
He can store hay for his animals, protect the water pipes and keep a machine to clear snow from the roads.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the problems of the temperate climate and how people adapt to them.

qa.q: In winter, snow and frost cover the ground for several months in the continental interiors. What problem does this cause for farmers?
qa.a: Crops cannot grow in winter, so the growing season is short. Animals must be kept inside and fed.

qa.q: In the 1930s, drought and strong winds blew away the soil of the American Prairies. What was this disaster called?
qa.a: It was called the Dust Bowl. Drought and bad farming left the soil bare, and the wind carried it away.

qa.q: In the hot, dry Mediterranean summer, what danger threatens forests and villages?
qa.a: Forest fires threaten them, for example in Greece, Spain and California.

qa.q: Farmers use a lot of fertilisers and pesticides. What problem can this cause?
qa.a: They can pollute rivers, lakes and underground water, and harm plants and animals.

sum.title: I. Problems Faced
sum.intro: The main problems faced in the temperate region are the following:
items: A. Cold Winters
Snow and frost make transport difficult, freeze water pipes and stop crops from growing.
B. Short Growing Season
In the cold interiors, crops can grow only from spring to autumn.
C. Drought and Soil Erosion
Drought and strong winds can blow away bare soil, as in the Dust Bowl of the American Prairies in the 1930s.
D. Storms, Floods and Forest Fires
Storms and floods hit western coasts. Forest fires burn Mediterranean lands in summer.
E. Pollution
The heavy use of fertilisers and pesticides pollutes rivers and underground water.

qa.q: How are houses in cold countries built to keep people warm in winter?
qa.a: They have thick insulated walls, double windows, heating systems and sloping roofs so that snow slides off.

qa.q: How can farmers grow vegetables in winter, when it is too cold outside?
qa.a: They grow them in greenhouses made of glass or plastic, which keep the heat of the sun inside.

qa.q: After the Dust Bowl, farmers planted rows of trees around their fields. Why?
qa.a: The rows of trees, called shelterbelts, break the force of the wind and protect the soil from erosion.

sum.title: II. Adaptations
sum.intro: People have adapted to the problems of the temperate region in the following ways:
items: A. Houses and Clothing
Houses have thick insulated walls, double windows, heating and sloping roofs. People wear coats, gloves and boots in winter.
B. Transport
Snowploughs clear the roads, and salt is spread to melt ice.
C. Farming Adaptations
Farmers use greenhouses, store hay for winter, grow winter wheat and irrigate in dry summers.
D. Soil Protection
Shelterbelts of trees, contour ploughing and crop rotation protect the soil from erosion.
E. Fighting Fires and Pollution
Firefighters, aircraft and firebreaks fight forest fires. Laws limit the use of fertilisers and pesticides.

evaluation: Give two problems caused by cold winters in the temperate region.
Snow blocks roads and frost stops crops from growing.
What is a greenhouse and why is it used?
A greenhouse is a building of glass or plastic that keeps heat inside. It is used to grow crops when it is too cold outside.
The Dust Bowl was a disaster in the American Prairies in the 1930s, when drought and wind blew away the soil.
remediation: Very cold nights that freeze the ground cause ______.
The soil erosion disaster of the American Prairies was the Dust ______.
In the Mediterranean summer, forests are threatened by ______.
A building of glass that keeps heat inside is a ______.
Rows of trees that protect soil from wind are called ______.
A machine that clears snow from roads is a ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. frost 2. Bowl 3. fires 4. greenhouse 5. shelterbelts 6. snowplough
